execution.progress: Arranging is paid work whose exact job and escrow persist across interruption; resume pays only remaining work and cancellation/death settles once. Inspect, trial-rest and remove are atomic.

details.costs: Arrange: inputStackId of owned moss, quantity in 0.1 steps (default 0.5) and an unoccupied ordinary-ground x/y within 0.65 plus body radius; two work rounds at one energy each. Resume/cancel use personal processId. Inspect: one round and 0.2 energy in reach. Trial-rest: stand on a completed, unoccupied patch; one ordinary rest round. Remove: the arranger only, unoccupied patch, one round and one energy.
details.effects: A completed patch holds the reserved material in a 0.25-radius footprint used only for occupancy and drawing; no thickness, coverage, body fit, warmth, insulation or comfort is inferred. Trial-rest runs the existing rest action unchanged and records energy before and after; the patch is not a registered facility, so it adds no recovery bonus. Inspect records visible placement, remaining quantity, occupancy and tests as a personal unverified record. Remove returns the remaining material as an owned stack at the site and deletes the patch; pickup stays a separate action. Cancel releases reserved material once; death releases it on the ground. Spent effort is never refunded. No reward, regrowth, repair or top-up.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 4000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form.
